children: fell 0.75% premarket as flights resumed across Britain after an air traffic control failure grounded 30% of scheduled departures on Tuesday. Cirium counts roughly 2,000 flights affected over two days. Ryanair cancelled 260, hitting 48,000 passengers, and puts its losses at 3 million so far. British Airways cancelled or diverted 100 on Tuesday and another 190 on Wednesday.

Ryanair says NATS told it the cause was the same rogue flight plan behind the 2023 shutdown, which cost airlines 100 million ($135 million). Michael O'Leary called it "an absolute rerun" and said NATS chief executive Martin Rolfe, in post since 2015, should be fired. Rolfe told BBC Radio the problem was not the same as 2023 and described something never seen in 50 years of operation, while ruling out a cyberattack. NATS didn't confirm the cause to Reuters.

Transport minister Heidi Alexander summoned Rolfe to explain, saying she wants assurances that lessons will be learned. There was also a radar fault in July 2025. NATS is a public-private partnership part-owned by British Airways, easyJet, pension funds and the government, and it paid its owners 175 million in dividends in 2025. Ryanair is suing it at the High Court for more than 7 million over the 2023 outage.

title: Ryanair Puts Its Outage Losses at 3 Million and Counting
